hints: Checking each 'O' group for 'does it touch the border?' is awkward. Which 'O's are definitely safe, and could you start from them instead?
Reverse the logic: flood fill (DFS) from every border 'O', marking those cells as safe (e.g. temporarily 'S'). Every 'O' that was not marked is trapped.

1. For every cell on the border that is 'O', flood fill and change connected 'O's to 'S'.
  2. Scan the whole board.
  3. Turn every remaining 'O' into 'X'.
  4. Turn every 'S' back into 'O'.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: For each 'O' group, flood fill it and check whether any cell is on the border, then flip it if not.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Flood fill only from the border to mark safe cells, then one pass flips the rest — simpler and still linear.

explain: In the first sample the only border 'O' is (3,1); its fill marks just that cell because its neighbours are 'X'. The group (1,1), (1,2), (2,2) is never reached from the border, so the final scan turns it into 'X', and (3,1) is restored to 'O'. A single-cell board [['O']] is all border, so nothing changes. Remember the function returns nothing — change board itself.
recognize: Regions that are 'enclosed' unless they touch the edge → flood fill from the border and flip whatever was not reached.
